title: Second Polish Republic
capsule: The Second Polish Republic (Rzeczpospolita Polska) was reconstituted on 11 November 1918 after 123 years of partition, its borders settled only after wars with Ukraine (1918–1919), Soviet Russia (1919–1921), and Germany and Lithuania over Silesia and Vilnius. Under Józef Piłsudski, who staged a coup in 1926 and governed as de facto authoritarian until his death in 1935, the state organized a multiethnic polity of Poles, Ukrainians, Belarusians, Jews, and Germans across 388,000 km². Nazi Germany invaded on 1 September 1939, followed by the Soviet Union on 17 September under the Molotov–Ribbentrop Pact; the government went into exile in London and the republic's territory was divided between the two occupiers, effectively ending its independent existence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Second Republic's borders are well established through the Treaty of Riga (1921) and other post-WWI settlements; minor disputed areas (Vilnius corridor, Teschen) are documented in detail.
